reviewer: Agent-assisted source and taxonomy desk review; not expert, legal or field certification

limits: All 19 exact-locality preserved-specimen results were enumerated. Fifteen are birds; four records with null class fields were reviewed by order, family, scientific name, catalog number and museum dataset as fish candidates.
The exact Pansipit River locality string was used; spelling variants, coordinate-only queries and records filed under Taal Lake or Balayan Bay were not searched.

All four selected records share one coordinate with no uncertainty value and carry geodetic-datum/institution/collection quality flags. Coordinates are retained in this review only for audit and are excluded from the app projection.
No measured salinity or exact river reach is present. No estuary, freshwater/brackish classification, river boundary or present-day presence is inferred.

dataset.title: Field Museum of Natural History (Zoology) Fish Collection
dataset.citation: Grant S, Webbink K, McMahan C (2022). Field Museum of Natural History (Zoology) Fish Collection. Version 13.13. Field Museum. Occurrence dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/alz7wu accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-10-23.
dataset.reuseScope: The GBIF dataset registry marks this occurrence dataset CC0-1.0. This review uses only the four selected factual occurrence records; no blanket validation of other dataset rows or multimedia is implied.

taxonomyReviews.independentStatus: Ambassis commersonii Cuvier 1828 is a synonym of Ambassis ambassis (Lacepède 1802)
Bathygobius mearnsi is treated as a synonym of Bathygobius cyclopterus

decision.rationale: Four distinct CC0 Field Museum preserved-specimen occurrence records explicitly carry the Pansipit River locality. Independent taxonomy checks resolve them to four accepted fish species; the two synonym records remain linked to their recorded names. The records are historical and share one unvalidated coordinate, so they support text-locality assertions only. Each occurrence quality flag remains attached to its record.
caveats: All four occurrence rows have class=null in GBIF and were reviewed as fish using the order, family, scientific name, specimen basis, catalog number and fish-collection dataset. Their families are Zenarchopteridae, Ambassidae and Gobiidae.

The same coordinate is present on all four records, no coordinate uncertainty is supplied, and GBIF marks the datum as assumed WGS84. It is excluded from the public projection; no exact site or map pin is displayed.

All records also carry institution-match-fuzzy and institution-collection-mismatch flags. Three rows carry recorded-date-mismatch; these are retained. The date precision is preserved exactly: 1933-12 for one record and 1933 for three records.
One occurrence name is mapped to Ambassis ambassis and one to Bathygobius cyclopterus as synonyms. Both recorded names and accepted names remain available in the evidence details.
The locality is assigned by exact GBIF text only. The records do not establish which river reach, an estuary, measured salinity, current presence, abundance or a complete Pansipit inventory.
The separate NFRDI landing-center survey summary is not used as the basis of these specimen assertions and remains a separate 2023 catch-composition source with access and reuse limits.

nonClaims: These are four database rows for four species, not four individual fish or an abundance estimate.
The 1933 records are historical specimen-locality evidence, not current presence or a complete river checklist.
No map point, river boundary, exact reach, estuary assignment, salinity label, legal fishing permission, safety, diet or bait advice is inferred.
The NFRDI 2023 landing-center summary is not merged into the specimen evidence.
